title: Patterns
description: Grouped file handling patterns. Related patterns are combined to avoid overwhelming learners.

blocks.text: This combines reading all records, counting records, and processing numeric values from a file.

slides.title: Use this pattern when the question asks you to:

blocks.title: Use this pattern when the question asks you to:
items: Count how many records are in a file
Calculate a total or average from file data

slides.title: Pattern 1 - Read and Process Records: Code pattern

blocks.text:
OPENFILE "File.txt" FOR READ

WHILE NOT EOF("File.txt")
    READFILE "File.txt", value
    // process value here
ENDWHILE

CLOSEFILE "File.txt"

slides.title: Read and total values
slides.problem: Read all sales from Sales.txt and calculate the total.
slides.code:
DECLARE sale, total : REAL

total <- 0

OPENFILE "Sales.txt" FOR READ

WHILE NOT EOF("Sales.txt")
    READFILE "Sales.txt", sale
    total <- total + sale
ENDWHILE

CLOSEFILE "Sales.txt"
OUTPUT total
slides.explanation: The same read-and-process structure can be adapted for count, total, average, max/min or conditional count.

slides.title: Try It - Read and Process
slides.task: A file called Payments.txt stores one payment per line. Read all payments and count how many payments are greater than 100.
slides.expectedAnswer:
DECLARE payment : REAL
DECLARE count : INTEGER

count <- 0

OPENFILE "Payments.txt" FOR READ

WHILE NOT EOF("Payments.txt")
    READFILE "Payments.txt", payment

    IF payment > 100 THEN
        count <- count + 1
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE

CLOSEFILE "Payments.txt"
OUTPUT count

slides.title: Use this pattern when the question asks you to:

slides.title: Pattern 2 - Search or Match Records: Code pattern

blocks.text:
found <- FALSE

WHILE NOT EOF("File.txt") AND found = FALSE
    READFILE "File.txt", value
    IF value = searchValue THEN

slides.title: Search for a student ID
slides.problem: Search StudentIDs.txt for a student ID entered by the user.
slides.code:
DECLARE studentID, searchID : STRING
DECLARE found : BOOLEAN

found <- FALSE
INPUT searchID

OPENFILE "StudentIDs.txt" FOR READ

WHILE NOT EOF("StudentIDs.txt") AND found = FALSE
    READFILE "StudentIDs.txt", studentID

    IF studentID = searchID THEN
        found <- TRUE
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE

CLOSEFILE "StudentIDs.txt"

IF found = TRUE THEN
    OUTPUT "Found"
ELSE
    OUTPUT "Not found"
ENDIF
slides.explanation: The loop stops when the end of file is reached or when the matching ID is found.

lessons.title: Pattern 3 - Read into Arrays then Process

slides.title: Pattern 3 - Read into Arrays then Process

blocks.text: This combines file handling with arrays. Use it when data must be stored and processed later.

slides.title: Use this pattern when the question asks you to:

blocks.title: Use this pattern when the question asks you to:
items: Load file data into an array
Read a file once, then process the array
Use parallel arrays for multi-field records

slides.title: Pattern 3 - Read into Arrays then Process: Code pattern

blocks.text:
count <- 0

WHILE NOT EOF("File.txt")
    count <- count + 1
    READFILE "File.txt", Values[count]
ENDWHILE

FOR i <- 1 TO count
    // process Values[i]
NEXT i

slides.title: Read marks into an array and find highest
slides.problem: Read marks from Marks.txt into an array, then find the highest mark.
slides.code:
DECLARE Marks : ARRAY[1:100] OF INTEGER
DECLARE count, i, highest : INTEGER

count <- 0

OPENFILE "Marks.txt" FOR READ

WHILE NOT EOF("Marks.txt")
    count <- count + 1
    READFILE "Marks.txt", Marks[count]
ENDWHILE

CLOSEFILE "Marks.txt"

highest <- Marks[1]

FOR i <- 2 TO count
    IF Marks[i] > highest THEN
        highest <- Marks[i]
    ENDIF
NEXT i

OUTPUT highest
slides.explanation: The file is loaded into an array first. Then a normal array processing pattern is used.

slides.title: Try It - Read into Array then Process
slides.task: Read integer values from Marks.txt into array Marks. Then output how many marks are 50 or above.
slides.expectedAnswer:
DECLARE Marks : ARRAY[1:100] OF INTEGER
DECLARE count, i, passCount : INTEGER

count <- 0
OPENFILE "Marks.txt" FOR READ
WHILE NOT EOF("Marks.txt")
    count <- count + 1
    READFILE "Marks.txt", Marks[count]
ENDWHILE
CLOSEFILE "Marks.txt"

passCount <- 0
FOR i <- 1 TO count
    IF Marks[i] >= 50 THEN
        passCount <- passCount + 1
    ENDIF
NEXT i

OUTPUT passCount

markScheme.criterion: Open file and loop to EOF to load array
Second loop processes loaded array elements only
Correct condition for marks >= 50 and increment pass counter

blocks.text: This combines reading from one file, checking a condition, and writing selected records to another file.

slides.title: Use this pattern when the question asks you to:

blocks.title: Use this pattern when the question asks you to:
items: Write all matching records to a new file
Create a file of failed students, accepted entries, high scores, or filtered records
Copy selected records from one file to another

slides.title: Pattern 4 - Filter and Write Records: Code pattern

blocks.text:
OPENFILE "Input.txt" FOR READ
OPENFILE "Output.txt" FOR WRITE

WHILE NOT EOF("Input.txt")
    READFILE "Input.txt", value
    IF condition THEN
        WRITEFILE "Output.txt", value
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE

CLOSEFILE "Input.txt"
CLOSEFILE "Output.txt"

slides.title: Write failed marks to a file
slides.problem: Read marks from Marks.txt and write marks below 50 to Failed.txt.
slides.code:
DECLARE mark : INTEGER

OPENFILE "Marks.txt" FOR READ
OPENFILE "Failed.txt" FOR WRITE

WHILE NOT EOF("Marks.txt")
    READFILE "Marks.txt", mark

    IF mark < 50 THEN
        WRITEFILE "Failed.txt", mark
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE

CLOSEFILE "Marks.txt"
CLOSEFILE "Failed.txt"
slides.explanation: Only marks that match the condition are written to the new file.

blocks.text: Some files contain more than one data item per record, such as a name and a mark. These must be read into separate variables or parallel arrays.

This pattern is often combined with searching, filtering, counting, or writing to another file.

blocks.text: Insert one new record into a sorted file while preserving order. This appears in 9618/22/M/J/23 Q8(b) (AddItem).

blocks.title: When to use this pattern
items: A new record must be inserted in the correct position
A new output file must be created
All existing records must be copied

slides.title: Pattern 6 - Ordered File Insertion (9618/22/M/J/23 Q8(b)): Code pattern

blocks.text:
Written <- FALSE

OPENFILE "OldFile.txt" FOR READ
OPENFILE "NewFile.txt" FOR WRITE

WHILE NOT EOF("OldFile.txt")
    READFILE "OldFile.txt", CurrentRecord

    IF Written = FALSE AND NewKey < CurrentKey THEN
        WRITEFILE "NewFile.txt", NewRecord
        Written <- TRUE
    ENDIF

    WRITEFILE "NewFile.txt", CurrentRecord
ENDWHILE

IF Written = FALSE THEN
    WRITEFILE "NewFile.txt", NewRecord
ENDIF

CLOSEFILE "OldFile.txt"
CLOSEFILE "NewFile.txt"

slides.title: Ordered insertion with single-write flag
slides.problem: Insert one new sorted record while copying existing file content to a new file.
slides.code:
Written <- FALSE

OPENFILE "OldFile.txt" FOR READ
OPENFILE "NewFile.txt" FOR WRITE

WHILE NOT EOF("OldFile.txt")
    READFILE "OldFile.txt", CurrentRecord

    IF Written = FALSE AND NewKey < CurrentKey THEN
        WRITEFILE "NewFile.txt", NewRecord
        Written <- TRUE
    ENDIF

    WRITEFILE "NewFile.txt", CurrentRecord
ENDWHILE

IF Written = FALSE THEN
    WRITEFILE "NewFile.txt", NewRecord
ENDIF

CLOSEFILE "OldFile.txt"
CLOSEFILE "NewFile.txt"
slides.explanation:
- Use a Boolean flag so the new record is written once only
- Compare the new record key with the current file record key
- Write the new record before the first larger key
- Still write every original record
- If no larger key is found, write the new record at the end

slides.title: Try It - Stock File Insertion
slides.task: Use 9618/22/M/J/23 Q8(b). Write pseudocode for AddItem(), which creates NewStock.txt from Stock.txt and inserts a valid new item in the correct ascending ItemNum position.
slides.expectedAnswer:
PROCEDURE AddItem(NewInfo : STRING)
    DECLARE NewItemNum, CurrentItemNum : STRING
    DECLARE CurrentInfo : STRING
    DECLARE Written : BOOLEAN

    NewItemNum <- LEFT(NewInfo, 4)
    Written <- FALSE

    OPENFILE "Stock.txt" FOR READ
    OPENFILE "NewStock.txt" FOR WRITE

    WHILE NOT EOF("Stock.txt")
        READFILE "Stock.txt", CurrentInfo
        CurrentItemNum <- LEFT(CurrentInfo, 4)

        IF Written = FALSE AND NewItemNum < CurrentItemNum THEN
            WRITEFILE "NewStock.txt", NewInfo
            Written <- TRUE
        ENDIF

        WRITEFILE "NewStock.txt", CurrentInfo
    ENDWHILE

    IF Written = FALSE THEN
        WRITEFILE "NewStock.txt", NewInfo
    ENDIF

    CLOSEFILE "Stock.txt"
    CLOSEFILE "NewStock.txt"
ENDPROCEDURE

markScheme.criterion: Extracts new ItemNum from new item information
Opens Stock.txt for READ and NewStock.txt for WRITE
Uses EOF loop to read existing records
Extracts and compares current ItemNum with new ItemNum
Writes new item before first larger ItemNum using a flag
Writes every existing record to NewStock.txt
Handles insertion at end and closes both files
